Similar functionality may be found in labs::multi_bounding_box, but the logic here is closer to the minimum number of computations for this simple case. Here is benchmark result with a very large input shape: round_to_cell_size until centroids: 0.011 seconds. Node graph on the right using multi_bounding_box: 29.273 seconds.

We want to turn our input shape (which may be multiple if merge_inputs is True) into a representation of boxes of the size specified in the input datatable. This will allow us to easily create instances for each face of these boxes. To do this, we first create a 3D grid of points within the entire input's bounds, with spacing defined by the datatable, and then remove points (i.e. cells) that are not within the input shape.
